category_description: Withdrawal timelines, symptoms, safety signals, and management considerations.
item_json: {"name":"Khat withdrawal or crash syndrome","description":"Lethargy, hypersomnia, depressed mood, anhedonia, craving, nightmares, psychomotor slowing, and irritability may begin 12-24 hours after cessation, peak at 2-4 days, and last 7-21 days.","management":"Gradual tapering, hydration, nutrition, sleep hygiene, CBT, and motivational interviewing.","safety_notes":"Urgently assess suicidal ideation or severe depression.","source_ref":"ENH-ADD-007","evidence_level":"Scientific observation"}

category_description: Withdrawal timelines, symptoms, safety signals, and management considerations.
item_json: {"name":"Alcohol withdrawal syndrome","description":"Sweating, tachycardia, tremor, nausea, hallucinations, seizures, and delirium tremens can begin 6-12 hours after cessation, peak at 24-72 hours, and last 5-10 days.","management":"Medical detoxification, symptom-guided benzodiazepines, thiamine, folate, electrolyte support, and seizure precautions.","safety_notes":"Delirium tremens, seizures, confusion, fever, or severe vomiting require emergency inpatient care.","source_ref":"ENH-ADD-008","evidence_level":"WHO Alcohol Withdrawal Guidelines"}

description: Comprehensive substance use patterns, dependence, harm reduction, withdrawal syndromes, interventions, prevention, and Ethiopian cultural context.
category_description: Withdrawal timelines, symptoms, safety signals, and management considerations.
item_json: {"name":"Nicotine withdrawal","description":"Craving, irritability, anxiety, sleep disturbance, appetite change, concentration difficulty, and low mood usually begin within hours, peak at 2-3 days, and improve over 3-4 weeks.","management":"Nicotine replacement, trigger planning, behavioral support, and cessation medicines when scientificly appropriate.","source_ref":"ENH-ADD-009","evidence_level":"WHO Tobacco Cessation"}

item_json: {"name":"Opioid withdrawal","description":"Muscle pain, diarrhea, cramping, agitation, insomnia, sweating, nausea, vomiting, tachycardia, and craving may begin 6-12 hours after heroin and last 5-14 days.","management":"Medication-assisted treatment with methadone or buprenorphine, Scientific support, and symptom management.","safety_notes":"Withdrawal is distressing; reduced tolerance after withdrawal increases overdose risk if use resumes.","source_ref":"ENH-ADD-010","evidence_level":"WHO Opioid Dependence Guidelines"}
